name: Warázu
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant, penultimate (penultimate stress)' rests on an explicit, unhedged rule statement ('recai sempre na penúltima sílaba', stress non-phonemic) in the only linguistic description of Warázu (Ramirez, Vegini & França 2017, first-hand fieldwork), which I downloaded and verified verbatim at §2.1, galley p. 9; the article repeats the characterization in §2.2.1, galley p. 9 (LIAMES 17(2):411-506)', and assign an strength of the evidence. Given 'sempre' and 'não tem valor fonêmico', the record could arguably be 'strict' rather than merely dominant, but nothing in the source contradicts the current classification. No better source exists or is likely to appear soon (4-5 speakers in 2017).

sources.citation: Ramirez, Vegini & Franca 2017, O warazu do Guapore, LIAMES 17(2):411-506, phonology section (full PDF re-read)
sources.quote: Como se vê pelos exemplos acima, o acento não tem valor fonêmico: recai sempre na penúltima sílaba.

sources.citation: Ramirez, Henri; Vegini, Valdir; França, Maria Cristina Victorino de. 2017. O warázu do Guaporé (tupi-guarani): primeira descrição linguística. LIAMES 17(2): 411-506. DOI 10.20396/liames.v17i0.8647468
sources.quote: 'O padrão silábico é (C)V ou (C)VV ... Como se vê pelos exemplos acima, o acento não tem valor fonêmico: recai sempre na penúltima sílaba. No entanto, pensando em futuras pesquisas, indicaremos quase sempre, neste estudo, o acento.' Later: 'Como língua tupi-guarani com acento na penúltima sílaba e de padrão silábico (C)V(V) sem sílabas fechadas...'
sources.locator: §2.1 'Realização dos fonemas e oposições', galley p. 9 (the text); restated txt l. 845 (§2.2, comparative discussion)

sources.citation: Danielsen, Swintha & Noé Gasparini. 2015. Discovering two almost extinct languages in Bolivia: Jorá and Guarasu. Communication, 18e Rencontres Jeunes Chercheurs en Sciences du Langage, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle - Paris 3, Paris, 11-12 June 2015. 14 pp. HAL hal-01495156, version 1 (deposited 2017-03-24). [Danielsen (ed.) 2021 Guarayu/Guarasu bibliography lists it as Danielsen&Gasparini2015 with year 2017 = deposit year.]

tone.quote: In Guarasu (as in Guarayo), the fricatives [j] and [ʒ] are free variants of one single phoneme, which complicates the whole analysis of graphemes. [...] For other reconstructed proto-phonemes, it is impossible to determine their representation in the languages. More complex aspects remain problematic, like the description of nasalization or the existence of final non-released consonants. Phonetic comparison was a first step but only gave insights and evidence for proximity. However, it provided no argument for classification.
tone.summary: No tone discussion; segmental grapheme-interpretation notes only. Consistent with (but does not state) the non-tonal Tupi-Guarani profile; the catalog's fixed-penultimate-stress statement still rests solely on Ramirez, Vegini & França 2017.

sources.citation: Danielsen, Swintha & Lena Sell (eds.). 2015. Diccionario Flora y Fauna Guarasu. Santa Cruz de la Sierra. (and any grammar notes from Danielsen/Sell/Terhart's Guarasu documentation project, Bolivian side)

sources.access_detail: a catalogue record only (no print holding to request from, no digital copy known)
sources.note: Only other modern first-hand material on the language (Bolivian Guarasu variety); would show whether an independent team marks stress consistently penultimate. Low value for the classification itself, which rests on an explicit rule statement.
